Verified_Outcome: Table 1 (n=17; mean ± SD; berberine/control geometric mean ratio and 90% CI): caffeine 93 mg probe. AUC0–∞ 33.98 ± 9.40 vs 29.80 ± 11.30 μg·h/mL; ratio 85% (76–95%). Cmax 4.48 ± 1.03 vs 4.16 ± 1.86 μg/mL; 88% (75–103%). Tmax 0.96 ± 0.45 vs 1.00 ± 0.41 h; 108% (86–135%). t1/2 5.41 ± 1.81 vs 4.75 ± 1.15 h; 89% (78–102%). Plasma caffeine/paraxanthine ratio at 6 h: 1.51 ± 2.06 vs 0.94 ± 0.45; 80% (59–108%). Results state there were no statistically significant PK differences; Table 1 shows no significance marker. The article notes caffeine AUC0–∞ and Cmax did not meet its 80–125% bioequivalence criterion, despite nonsignificance, and cites small sample size as a possible explanation. This result is not evidence of equivalence or absence of effect.
Remaining_Limitation: One small study in healthy young Chinese men (17 completers), one 14-day berberine-capsule regimen and one 93-mg caffeine probe. Nonsignificance does not prove no effect; reported caffeine AUC/Cmax 90% CIs do not lie wholly within 80–125% equivalence bounds. Berberine capsule salt/content/excipients and coffee beverage matrix are not fully characterized. Not an ordinary dietary interaction study or dose-equivalence assessment.
